newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps hold amid falling crude, for now.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps hold amid falling crude, for now.

text.p: European oil swaps held their own on Thursday amidst a tumbling screen market but dealers said levels would probably ease off tomorrow if crude's slide went unchecked.
Brent CFDs were a touch firmer with July 7-11 assessed at +7 cents against August Brent compared with +1 cent on Wednesday.
July 14-18 was put at -10 cents against August from -13/14 cents while July 21-25 was only one cent stronger at -14 cents.
Trades were done for July 14-18 at September -18 cents and for July 21-August 01 at September -28 cents.
Heavy fuel climbed and then dipped finishing the day close to where it started.

Dealers said July swaps were done at $84.50 and $85.00 before crude's slide when the market eased back to $83.50/$84.00 bid with no offers heard. 4Q was thought done at $93.00 with offers subsequently at $92.00.
Gasoline swaps resisted crude's draw lower, although dealers questioned for how long.
"If crude continues to fall, gasoline will have to react by going lower," said one dealer. Swaps were heard traded at $188.50 for July and $187.50 for August at least two times.

Naphtha also appeared immune to crude's weakness, although traders conceded that a lack of players in the market today was partly responsible for the sideways movement. Deals were done around $175 on July with August and September contangoed by $1/1.50 and $2/2.50 respectively.
